changes.sense: Empty in empty set: the set has no elements and is denoted by ∅. This is not the empty string, the number zero, or a singleton containing ∅.
changes.rationale: Retain الخالية in المجموعة الخالية. After reading the academy notation book, physical PDF p. 96 / printed p. 84, I verified that its ∅ row is labelled إشارة المجموعة الخالية. This directly supports the Arabic nomenclature attached to the same symbol; it is not an English-Arabic dictionary entry. EN OLP-0005 L15–17 defines the set by having no elements. MSA L15–17 says لا تحتوي على أي عناصر, and Classical L15–16 says ليس لها عناصر, with الخالية agreeing with المجموعة. Those negative membership conditions preserve the source sense; the adjective does not describe a zero-valued member or an empty string. The evidence therefore supports retaining this particular term and its defining phrase in both editions, not certifying every use of empty. This is a new retrospective assessment, not evidence that the original translator consulted this book.

witnesses.excerpt:
A \emph{set} is a collection of objects, considered {as} a single
object. The objects making up the set are called \emph{elements} or
\emph{members} of the set. If $x$ is !!a{element} of a set~$A$, we
write $x \in A$; if not, we write $x \notin A$. The set which has no
!!{element}s is called the \emph{empty} set and
denoted~``$\emptyset$''.

changes.sense: Intersection of two arbitrary sets A and B: exactly the elements belonging to both; membership is the conjunction x∈A ∧ x∈B. It may be empty.
changes.rationale: Retain التقاطع as the definition label. I first read the academy notation book, physical PDF p. 95 / printed p. 83, section (5), where إشارة التقاطع names ∩ and the adjacent explanation specifies العناصر المشتركة. The book's common-members sense matches EN OLP-0008 L71–79, not merely the ordinary geometric idea of two lines crossing. The MSA definition at L70–78 says membership in كل من A وB; the Classical definition at L65–73 says membership in A وB معًا. Each is immediately fixed by the unchanged conjunction in the set-builder formula, and each permits an empty intersection. The noun is therefore retained for a specific set-theoretic reason and actual target-language evidence. This consultation was retrospective; the notation book does not establish medieval usage or certify the English-Arabic dictionary mapping.
changes.expert_question: At OLP-0008, MSA L70–78 and Classical L65–73, does التقاطع plus كل من / معًا clearly mean simultaneous membership in both arbitrary sets, including the empty case, without suggesting only geometric crossings? هل يحفظ التعريف شرط الانتماء إلى المجموعتين معًا، ولو لم يوجد بينهما عنصر مشترك؟

witnesses.excerpt:
\begin{defn}[Intersection]
The \emph{intersection} of two sets $A$ and $B$, written $A \cap B$, is
the set of all things which are !!{element}s of both $A$ and~$B$.
\[
A \cap B = \Setabs{x}{x \in A \land x \in B}
\]
Two sets are called \emph{disjoint} if their intersection is
empty. This means they have no !!{element}s in common.
\end{defn}

changes.sense: Union of two sets A and B: all elements belonging to A or to B, including elements in both; membership is inclusive disjunction, not exclusive disjunction or addition of multiplicities.
changes.rationale: Retain الاتحاد as the definition label. Before assessing the wording, I read the academy notation book, physical PDF p. 95 / printed p. 83, section (5): إشارة الاتحاد names ∪ and its explanation expressly includes المشتركة وغير المشتركة. That is target-language evidence for this inclusive set operation, matching EN OLP-0008 L34–40. MSA L33–39 and Classical L30–36 both expressly include membership in A or B or both, using أو كلتيهما and the formula x∈A ∨ x∈B; the heading therefore covers shared elements as well as elements in only one set. The later source example states that a common element is counted once, so the explanatory جمع language must not be read as numerical addition or multiset sum. The academy's specific label is retained while the inclusive condition remains explicit. This is retrospective source-grounded retention, not a claim about earlier consultation, medieval usage, or official bilingual dictionary certification.

A \cup B = \Setabs{x}{x \in A \lor x \in B}
\]
\end{defn}
